method: Separate persistent workers, frozen baseline Python, original/candidate native PE; sequential GPU/CPU calls; nonexclusive host.
scope: Persistent pool N->N/2->N for uniform/prior PR posterior, and continuous five predict/PR/ESS/conditional resample/estimate/migration epochs; resident runtimes. Full-state get/set and PR controls unchanged. Initialization/restoration/IPC/hash/input setup excluded.
warmups: One call per batch, or one call per process per paired round; each timed call is restored first.

traced_host_peak_measurements.scope: Python/NumPy traced peak increment during public migration; input/init/restore/hash/snapshots excluded; C++ vector and GPU allocations not traced.

change: For existing all-finite equal-weight resident pool migration, construct the exact original sequential FP64 cumsum(1/N) on GPU. A bounded CPU descriptor list advances positive FP64 bit patterns by constant integer ULP increments within exponent bins; odd tie cases and exponent crossings execute the original FP64 addition. The GPU reconstructs every CDF element using integer arithmetic and bitcast only. Original exact left search/clamp/all16 gather/weight kernels remain unchanged. Reuse source CDF and target ancestor-B scratch; upload only the descriptor list, no new CUDA allocations or owners. Runtime requires original checked-CDF hook pair, native/public count agreement, default NumPy policy and full finite/equal validation. Small source/target, non-nearest CPU rounding, in-place/cross-device, unsupported hosts and old/injected/overridden backends retain original fallback. Same FP64/CDF bits/model/count/RNG/tolerances.
